fact_en: The ribs protect your lungs and heart, and the rib cage spreads a little each time you breathe in to make room for air.
fact_bis: Ang mga gusok manalipod sa baga ug kasingkasing, ug mobukha gamay ang rib cage matag moginhawa ka aron adunay luna ang hangin.

findings.note: title_bis "Gukod nga Bantay sa Baga" for "Ribs Guard the Lungs". "Gukod" means to chase/pursue in Cebuano; ribs are "gusok" — which the body itself uses correctly ("Ang mga gusok manalipod sa baga"). Lower severity because the body restores the fact, but the title as shipped names an action, not the bone, and looks like a corrupted gusok.

fact_en:
Why do clams bury in sand?

Clams dig down into sand or mud underwater and bury themselves there to hide.
fact_bis:
Nganong naglubong ang halaan sa balas?

Ang halaan magkalot ug maglubong sa iyang kaugalingon sa balas o lapok ilalom sa tubig aron motago.

findings.note: title_bis "Nangalumos nga Halaan" for "Burrowing Clams". "Lumos" = to drown (same root used correctly in ffct-00429 "Lumos sa Mabaw nga Tubig"), not to burrow/bury — the body correctly says "magkalot ug maglubong sa iyang kaugalingon sa balas". Body restores the fact, so low severity, but the headline tells the child the clams are drowning.

fact_en: Wasps are most likely to sting when you get close to their nest, so it's best to stay away and leave it alone.
fact_bis: Mas posible mosundot ang putakti kon duol ka sa ilang salag, busa maayo nga magpalayo ug dili kini hilabtan.

findings.note: Wasp card titled with the wrong insect: title_bis "Salag sa Putyokan" = honeybee's nest, but the card is about wasps (en title "Wasp Nest"; body correctly says "putakti"). Same class of defect as the cat card titled `iro`: the heading names a different animal than the card teaches, so a child skimming titles learns bees sting near their nest. Body text is otherwise accurate.

fact_en:
Why does a male cricket sing?

To attract a female cricket to be his mate.
fact_bis:
Nganong mag-awit ang lalaki nga kagang?

Aron danihon ang baye nga kagang isip kapikas.

findings.note: Body calls the cricket `kagang` twice ("Nganong mag-awit ang lalaki nga kagang... danihon ang baye nga kagang"). `kagang` is a small crab in Cebuano — the repo's own Cebuano prose uses it that way ("ang umang — ang gagmayng kagang sa baybayon", "ang kagang adunay shell nga adunay mga tunok"). Only title_bis says `kuliglig`, so the body never corrects itself: a child reads that male crabs sing to attract females. Cricket is `gangis`/`kuliglig` (both already used elsewhere in the corpus). Corpus-wide the swap hits 9 cards (ffct-01825, ffct-01874, ffct-03568, ffct-03598, ffct-03727, ffct-04846, ffct-11883, ffct-11910), several with no cricket word anywhere to restore it.

fact_en:
How does a wasp sting deliver venom?

It pushes its stinger into your skin, and a venom sac inside squeezes the venom in — like a tiny, super-fast injection!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagsulod sa hilo sa putyukan?

Isulod niini ang tibo sa imong panit, unya mopuga ang sudlanan sa hilo aron iduso kini — sama sa gamay, paspas kaayo nga iniksyon!

findings.note: Card is about a WASP sting ('How does a wasp sting deliver venom?'). The Cebuano body asks 'Unsaon pagsulod sa hilo sa PUTYUKAN?' — putyukan is the honeybee, a different insect. The corpus itself draws that distinction: ffct-03517 bis reads 'Ang putakti ug hornet dili maghimo og dugos — ang tam-is nga dugos gikan ra sa putyukan' (wasps/hornets make no honey; honey comes only from the putyukan), and this card's own tl says 'putakti'. Nothing in the Cebuano card corrects it: title_bis is 'Tibo sa Kagitgit', which never repeats putakti, so a child reading only the Cebuano learns this is about bees. Body-level species swap, not a wording nit.

fact_en: A rabbit uses its back teeth to grind grass, and this wears those teeth down over time.
fact_bis: Gigamit sa kuneho ang likod nga ngipon aron galingon ang sagbot, nga mao usab maghait niini sa paglabay sa panahon.

findings.note: EN: grinding grass "wears those teeth down over time". BIS says the opposite: "nga mao usab maghait niini sa paglabay sa panahon" = it SHARPENS them over time. The wearing-down fact is the whole point of the card and nothing in the Cebuano restores it; a child reads that chewing grass sharpens the rabbit's back teeth.

fact_en:
What's the most poisonous part of a pufferfish?

In a female pufferfish, the eggs and inner organs are among the most poisonous parts — which is why they're especially dangerous to eat.
fact_bis:
Unsa ang labing makahilo nga bahin sa butete?

Sa baye nga butete, ang itlog ug pipila ka bahin sa sulod maoy uban sa labing makahilo nga parte — mao nga labi kining delikado kan-on.

findings.note: title_bis "Itlog sa Baboy-Dagat" names a different animal: baboy-dagat is the dugong/sea cow (the corpus itself uses it that way in ffct-03453 terms: dugong/duyong/baboy-dagat/sea-cow). The card is about pufferfish (butete, as the body correctly says), and dugongs are mammals that do not lay eggs, so the heading teaches a false name-to-animal mapping.

fact_en:
Why does a wasp sting burn?

A wasp sting feels like fire because the venom triggers pain nerves straight to your brain—it is not actually hot, your body is just tricked!
fact_bis:
Nganong murag nagdilaab ang tusok sa putyukan?

Murag nagdilaab ang tusok sa putyukan kay ang hilo maglihok sa mga nerbiyos nga magdala og kasakit ngadto sa utok—dili gyud kini init, ang lawas lang gilimbongan!

findings.note: Card is about a WASP sting, but both the Cebuano question and answer say `putyukan` (honeybee) - "Nganong murag nagdilaab ang tusok sa putyukan?". Its own title_bis says `Tambuboan` (wasp), so the card names two different insects and the body never corrects itself. Lower-confidence flag: the science (venom triggers pain nerves, not real heat) stays true for bees, and some speakers use `putyukan` loosely for stinging insects - but the corpus itself distinguishes them, using `putakti`/`tambubuk`/`alumindig` for wasp (ffct-00325, ffct-01604, ffct-02130, ffct-04292) and `putyukan` for bee (ffct-01268, ffct-01309, ffct-01331). Note ffct-00767, ffct-03518 and ffct-03786 make the same wasp->putyukan substitution, so the grep will hit a cluster.

fact_en:
Why can't you just plant a Rafflesia in a garden?

A Rafflesia needs the special vine it lives inside to survive — that's why it's so hard to grow anywhere outside the forest!
fact_bis:
Nganong dili nimo lang matanom ang Rafflesia sa hardin?

Nagkinahanglan ang Rafflesia sa espesyal nga liana nga ginapuy-an niini aron mabuhi — mao nga lisod kaayo kini patubuon gawas sa lasang!

findings.note: title_bis "Rafflesia Kinahanglan ug Ubas" — `ubas` is GRAPES, not a host vine (`baging`/`liana`/`balagon`, as the terms list and the body's `liana` show). Title asserts the Rafflesia needs grapes.

fact_en: Your body doesn't need everything perfectly the same inside — it just keeps conditions within a narrow, safe range.
fact_bis: Dili kinahanglan nga hingpit nga parehas ang kahimtang sa sulod sa imong lawas; ginapabilin lang kini sa sulod sa pig-ot ug luwas nga sakup.

findings.note: title_bis "Bali sa Sulod sa Lawas" — `bali` in Cebuano reads as fracture/break (or reverse), not `balanse` (the term list has `balanse`). Title announces something broken inside the body; body text is correct about a narrow safe range. Title-only defect, lower severity than the others.

fact_en:
How do ants find food?

Ants leave a pheromone trail—a chemical scent—along their path, so other ants can follow it straight to the food!
fact_bis:
Giunsa pagpangita og pagkaon sa langgam?

Ang mga langgam nagbiya og pheromone sa ilang dalan—usa ka kemikal nga aroma—aron masundan kini sa ubang langgam ngadto sa pagkaon!

findings.note: Whole body is about ANTS in English but says `langgam` three times in Cebuano — in Cebuano `langgam` is a BIRD (the Tagalog false friend: TL langgam = ant). Card reads "Giunsa pagpangita og pagkaon sa langgam? Ang mga langgam nagbiya og pheromone...", so a Cebuano child learns that birds lay pheromone trails. Only title_bis (`Hantik`) is right; the body never says ant (hulmigas/hantik/subay). Unrecoverable.

fact_en:
Why do you feel pain after pulling away?

Your brain only finds out about a reflex after it's already happened — that's why you feel the pain even though your body already reacted!
fact_bis:
Ngano mabati nimo ang sakit human ka mahilak?

Ang utok mahibalo lang sa reflex human na kini mahitabo — mao nga mabati nimo ang sakit bisan human na molihok ang imong lawas!

findings.note: Question renders "after pulling away" as "human ka mahilak" = after you CRY. The withdrawal reflex — the whole setup of the card — is gone, so the posed question (why pain after crying?) is not what the answer explains.
